inputs.text: In Palakkad on March 28, Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan dismissed allegations of Rs 700 crore corruption over the proposed Cooperative Department software project as “political.” That may be true of the accusations, but it is no substitute for answering them. Cooperative members and ordinary people should not bear the cost of opaque decisions about systems and money they depend on. The government owes them clear disclosure and accountability; treating scrutiny as a political fight risks protecting institutions from questions instead of protecting the public.
